In a study19 of 46 patients on warfarin who had been converted from pravastatin to simvastatin, the mean INR increased, but the median weekly warfarin dose did not differ significantly and no episodes of bleeding were report- ed. Dextrothyroxine increases the anticoagulant effect of warfarin sodium20,21 and dicoumarol.22 Colestyramine has reduced warfarin’s serum concentration23 and half-life24 as well as its activity.23,24 The mechanisms of this in- teraction include binding of warfarin to colestyramine and re- duced absorption;23 the enterohepatic recycling of warfarin may also be interrupted.24 Phenprocoumon’s activity has also been re- duced by colestyramine.25 However, colestyramine can also re- duce vitamin K absorption, and this may result in hypoprothrom- binaemia and bleeding. Use of omega-3 fatty acids (as fish oil preparations) in patients taking warfarin and other antithrombotics has been associated with INR elevation26 and subdural haematoma.27 However, con- trolled studies in patients taking fish oil and warfarin28,29 have failed to show an effect on bleeding episodes or bleeding time.
